headline: Netanyahu warns Iran may try to disrupt Israel election
dek: Netanyahu warned Iran may try to disrupt Israel's Oct 27 general election ('don't test us'), days after he said (Wednesday) he had sent a directive to Israel's security forces to topple Iran's clerical state, and a day after Trump issued his second endorsement urging Israelis to vote for…
sources: Benjamin Netanyahu X post (@netanyahu, Oct 25) via SCMP
fault_line: Election-eve warning or wartime politics -- is Tehran really planning to disrupt the vote, or is the threat the message?

sections.what_happened: Netanyahu warned Iran may try to disrupt Israel's Oct 27 general election ('don't test us'), days after he said (Wednesday) he had sent a directive to Israel's security forces to topple Iran's clerical state, and a day after Trump issued his second endorsement urging Israelis to vote for Netanyahu. SCMP also reports Trump has sent a third aircraft carrier strike group toward the Persian Gulf and that US strikes could resume after the Nov 3 midterms.
sections.what_verified: Primary source (Netanyahu's own X post) + SCMP (T3) reporting. Trump's endorsement was already recorded at 0700-05 today; the election-disruption warning itself was not in any prior scan.
sections.what_disputed: No evidence presented in-window of an actual Iranian disruption plot -- the warning is a statement of intent/deterrence, not a confirmed plot. Army chief Lt Gen Eyal Zamir reportedly noted privately that a strike before the election was not operationally required (The Week, Oct 25). Opposition figures frame the Trump endorsement as a sign of desperation (Axios via 0700 record).
sections.why_matters: One day before Israel votes, Netanyahu warns Tehran: don't test us -- while Trump tells Israelis to vote for him.
sections.context: Background: Netanyahu warns Iran may try to disrupt Israel election: 'don't test us'
